lead: New Jersey plumbing deals with old housing, lead service lines, basement flooding and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from North Jersey to the Shore.
risk: lead and galvanized pipes in older homes, basement flooding and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, flooding and frozen pipes
why: New Jersey has a lot of older housing, and lead service lines are still being replaced in many towns under a state law that requires utilities to replace them. Older homes in Newark, Jersey City and Paterson also have galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains.
Heavy storms, like Ida in 2021, flood basements and back up sewers. Shore towns face coastal flooding. Winters freeze pipes. The State Board of Examiners of Master Plumbers licenses plumbers.
tips: Ask your water utility what your service line is made of.
Test your sump pump and consider a battery backup.
Ask about a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
areas: Calls come from Newark, Jersey City, Paterson, Elizabeth, Trenton, Camden, Central Jersey and the Jersey Shore.

faq.q: Is my New Jersey water line made of lead?
faq.a: It might be if your home is older. New Jersey requires water utilities to find and replace lead service lines, and many have online lookups. A plumber can also check where the line enters your house.
